summary: Interpreted the child receipt (ca11633cbde949dba0da0b9950651148, exit 0, test passed): all four vote comparisons are complete and hold — one identical RequestVote (term 4, candidate claim (82, term 2), leadership-transfer flag) was granted by the phantom holder (claim (82, term 2) over its installed snapshot at 63/term 3) and rejected by the majority voter whose claim matched its snapshot (63, term 3), so the same request produced different decisions and the granted authority rested on entries the voter's own snapshot superseded. The vote-decision half of @q_phantom_claim_vote_decision is therefore decided, and this turn attacks the remaining reachability half: the harness gained a configuration-change probe that runs the same validated five-voter phantom history and then removes either a phantom voter (leaving three consistent voters in the new quorum) or a consistent follower (leaving a quorum that needs a phantom acknowledgment), both issued on the majority leader and awaited for five seconds. Local construction runs showed the asymmetry — phantom removal committed immediately, consistent removal did not commit within the five-second window under identical history, snapshot index, timing and leader load — which gives an operational consequence of the starvation and supports the argument that the steps shrinking the voter set toward the phantom group are themselves blocked, so the phantom grant cannot be converted into authority over committed entries through a configuration change. A source range for appendConfigurationEntry was declared so the requirement carries a verified anchor. Still open: the config-change receipt (requested this turn), the source-derived second-order wedge that a stuck configuration entry closes the leader's change gate, and configuration changes attempted before the phantom state arises.
